scheme_name: Group Supply Of Goats And Sheep
description:
The Group Supply of Goats and Sheep scheme is an initiative launched by the Government of India to enhance the livelihood of rural households.

This scheme was introduced in the year 2014 under the National Livestock Mission.

The primary objective of this scheme is to promote goat and sheep rearing as a sustainable source of income for rural families.

The scheme aims to provide financial assistance to groups of farmers for the purchase of goats and sheep.

The target is to empower at least 1 lakh families across various states by the end of the financial year 2025.

The scheme also seeks to improve the genetic quality of livestock in the country.

It aims to increase the availability of quality meat and wool in the market.

The total budget allocated for this scheme is approximately INR 300 crores over a span of five years.

Under this scheme, each group of farmers can receive financial assistance of up to INR 1.5 lakh.

This amount is intended to cover the costs associated with purchasing goats and sheep.

The scheme provides for the establishment of a minimum of 10 to 15 members in each group.

Eligibility for participation in this scheme is primarily limited to small and marginal farmers.

Farmers must belong to rural areas and have a minimum landholding of 0.5 hectares.

The age limit for beneficiaries is set between 18 to 60 years.

The income criteria stipulate that the annual income of the household should not exceed INR 1.5 lakh.

Educational qualifications are not a mandatory requirement for participation in this scheme.

The application process begins with the formation of a group of eligible farmers.

Interested farmers must submit an application to the local Animal Husbandry Department.

The application should include details such as the number of members in the group and their respective landholdings.

Farmers must also provide identification documents such as Aadhar cards and bank account details.

Once the application is submitted, it is reviewed by the district level committee.

The committee assesses the feasibility of the project based on the proposed number of livestock.

If approved, the committee will issue a sanction order for the financial assistance.

The disbursement of funds is typically made in two installments.

The first installment is released upon approval of the project.

The second installment is released after the group successfully purchases the goats and sheep.

The timeline for the entire application process can take anywhere from 30 to 60 days.

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries Animal Husbandry and Dairying.

The contact details for the Department of Animal Husbandry can be found on their official website.

The scheme also emphasizes the importance of training and capacity building for the beneficiaries.

Training programs are organized to educate farmers about proper animal husbandry practices.

These programs cover aspects such as feeding, breeding, and health management of goats and sheep.

The scheme encourages the use of local breeds which are better adapted to the climatic conditions.

It also promotes the establishment of community-based breeding programs.

The expected outcome of the scheme is an increase in the income of participating families by at least 30 percent.

The scheme aims to create a sustainable livelihood option that can be passed on to future generations.

The government also collaborates with various NGOs and cooperatives to facilitate the implementation of the scheme.

Monitoring and evaluation of the scheme are conducted at regular intervals to assess its impact.

The government has set a target to increase the population of goats and sheep by 20 percent by 2025.

This is expected to contribute significantly to the overall livestock population in the country.

The scheme is part of a larger strategy to boost the rural economy and reduce poverty.

It also aims to enhance food security by increasing the availability of meat and dairy products.

The government has also introduced a subsidy component to encourage farmers to adopt this practice.

The subsidy can cover up to 50 percent of the total cost of purchasing livestock.

This financial support is crucial for small farmers who may not have access to credit.

The scheme has been well received in various states such as Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra.

These states have reported a significant increase in goat and sheep rearing activities.

The government has also established a helpline for beneficiaries to address their queries.

Farmers can contact the helpline for assistance with the application process and other related issues.

The scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in the rural sector.

It is also anticipated to enhance the nutritional status of rural households through increased meat consumption.

The government encourages the formation of self-help groups to facilitate collective action among farmers.

These groups can also assist in marketing the produce from goat and sheep rearing.

The scheme has the potential to contribute to the overall development of rural infrastructure.

It encourages the establishment of veterinary clinics and feed supply centers.

The government is committed to ensuring that the benefits of the scheme reach the intended beneficiaries.

Regular workshops and seminars are conducted to raise awareness about the scheme.

The Group Supply of Goats and Sheep scheme is a significant step towards improving rural livelihoods.

It aligns with the government's vision of doubling farmers' income by 2022.

The scheme reflects the government's commitment to sustainable agricultural practices.

It also emphasizes the importance of livestock in the rural economy.

The success of the scheme will depend on the active participation of farmers and local communities.

The government continues to monitor the progress of the scheme and make necessary adjustments.

This ensures that it remains relevant and effective in achieving its objectives.
